idiom_name: HttpClient + resilience4j Retry with a stable Idempotency-Key
implementation_notes: java.net.http.HttpClient (Java 11) sends the request while a retry decorator - resilience4j's Retry around a Supplier/CheckedSupplier, or Spring Retry's RetryTemplate - owns the attempt policy; HttpRequest builders produce immutable requests, so the Idempotency-Key must be attached to a request object that is built once and re-sent, or rebuilt with the same key value. resilience4j retries exceptions by default, so an HTTP 500 that arrives as a normal HttpResponse is not retried until retryOnResult says so, which is a feature: you decide which failures are replays. The decorator plus the JDK client replace the hand-written loop; the key, its persistence and the receiver-side record remain the application's contract.
pitfalls: The key must be created outside the decorated supplier; UUID.randomUUID() inside the lambda mints a new key for every retry.
resilience4j retries exceptions, not status codes - a 409 or 500 arrives as an ordinary return value, so configure retryOnResult deliberately and never replay 4xx business rejections.
sendAsync returns a CompletableFuture: composing a retry needs thenCompose/handle over the same request instance, and re-subscribing with a freshly built request is where new keys sneak in.

variants.name: gRPC Java channel with enableRetry() and a service-config retry policy
variants.implementation_notes: gRPC Java exposes the same service-config retryPolicy, switched on at the channel with ManagedChannelBuilder.enableRetry(): the client library then replays calls whose failures match the configured status codes, applying exponential backoff and retry throttling. As on every transport, the replay is not idempotency - the request message still needs an operation id for the server to dedupe - so keep the policy narrow (UNAVAILABLE and friends) and reserve it for mutations that carry the id.
pitfalls: Replaying a call whose message carries no operation id is a duplicate write; enableRetry() only decides when a call is re-sent.
Retry configuration is per method in the service config, so a broad policy for the whole service also replays mutations you never classified as idempotent.
